summary: Giuseppe Tucci was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Rome under Carlo Formichi and Giovanni Vacca, and later at Visva-Bharati University. He was a professor at Rome and president of the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East.

Giuseppe Vignato works in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies at Peking University under Angela Falco Howard, Chongfeng Li, Su Bai, and Shichang Ma, and held a post at Peking University attested in 2017.

Giyu Nishi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Taiken Kimura, Hakuju Ui, Sylvain Lévi, and others. He worked at the University of Tokyo and became a professor at Toyo University in 1927.

Glenn H. Mullin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous traditional Tibetan teachers, including Ling Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and Tenzin Gyatso, and founded The Mystical Arts of Tibet in 1984.
Glenn Wallis is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied under Masatoshi Nagatomi and the traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.
Gnanawimala Chandima is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Godabarish Mishra was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at Ravenshaw College and the University of Calcutta, taught at Satyabadi Bana Bidyalaya, served as headmaster at Chakradharpur High School, and became Director at the University of Madras.

Gombojab Tsybikov was a Tibetologist and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied medicine at Tomsk State University and oriental studies at the University of Saint Petersburg, later serving as a Lecturer of the Mongolian Language at Far Eastern Federal University (circa 1902–1917).

Gopinath Kaviraj was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at Maharaja's College, Jaipur, and the University of Allahabad under Arthur Venis and others. He served as librarian, principal, and Head of Yoga-Tantra at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Gordon D. Kaufman was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. Educated at Bethel College, Northwestern, and Yale University, he taught at Pomona College and Vanderbilt University before serving as Mallinckrodt Professor of Divinity at Harvard University.

Gordon Hannington Luce was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and linguistics. He was educated at Emmanuel College, Cambridge, and served as a professor at the University of Rangoon from circa 1923 to 1964.

Gordon Johnson is a historian and Indologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served as President of Wolfson College, Cambridge (1993–2010), Deputy Vice-Chancellor of Cambridge, and President of the Royal Asiatic Society (2015–2018).

Gottfried Ernst Groddeck was a scholar of linguistics and history. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne and held a post at Vilnius University from circa 1804 to 1824.

Gottfried Hermann was a linguist who studied at the universities of Leipzig and Jena. He spent his career at the University of Leipzig, serving as professor of philosophy and director of the philological seminar from 1803 to 1848.
Gottfried Kinkel was a historian who studied at the University of Bonn. He held academic posts at the University of Bonn (circa 1837–1848) and at ETH Zurich (circa 1866–1882).

Gotthilf Heinrich von Schubert was a philosopher who studied at the universities of Leipzig and Jena. He held academic posts at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (circa 1819–1827) and the University of Munich (circa 1827–1860).

Gottlieb Siegfried Bayer was a scholar of Sinology, history, and linguistics. Educated at the University of Königsberg, he held posts at the university and its cathedral before serving as a professor at the Imperial Academy of Sciences (1726–1737).

Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner was a linguist and Indologist who studied at King's College London and Heidelberg. He taught at King's College London, was Principal of Government College, Lahore, and was the first Registrar of the University of the Punjab.

Govind Chandra Pande was an Indologist and historian who studied under Kshetresa Chandra Chattopadhyaya. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Rajasthan, professor at the University of Allahabad, and chairman of both the Allahabad Museum and the Indian Institute of Advanced Study.

Govind Sadashiv Ghurye was an Indologist and sociologist. He studied at Elphinstone College and the University of Cambridge under W. H. R. Rivers and Alfred Cort Haddon, later heading the Department of Sociology at the University of Mumbai (1924–1959).
